title: Cap. IV Arg. 1 Sol: second — not every revealed placitum is the high Pauline predestination
pass_a_gloss: Second, that also is to be weighed: In our present controversy Theologians have never understood by the decree of predestination any pleasure of the Divine will whatsoever concerning the salvation and ruin of men, conceived under any form and revealed in the word. For if one is pleased to twist this word thither, the very decree of predestination itself will be contained in those words of Matt. 25:34 etc. The King will say to those who are on the right, Come, blessed of my Father, possess the kingdom prepared for you from the foundations of the world laid. For I hungered and you gave me what to eat, etc. He will say to those who will be on the left, Depart, cursed, into eternal fire, which is prepared for the devil and his angels. For I hungered, and you did not give me what to eat, etc. The decree of predestination will also be expressed in those at Rom. 2:6. God will render to each according to his works: to those indeed who persist, glory and honor and immortality of good work: but to those who are contentious, and who do not obey the truth, but obey injustice, heat and wrath will be rendered, etc. For in these and similar places the will of God concerning the salvation and ruin of men is opened to us, and yet to place in such decrees that high and inscrutable predestination which Paul so greatly celebrates and admires is most alien from the sense and sentence of the Scriptures, and of all sound Theologians.
pass_b_english: Second: in our controversy theologians have never meant by the predestination decree any revealed pleasure of the divine will about men's salvation and ruin, under any form. Twist the word that way and Matt. 25:34ff. itself becomes the decree — Come, blessed of my Father… Depart, cursed… — and so does Rom. 2:6, God will render to each according to his works. Those places do open God's will about salvation and ruin; but to lodge in them that high, inscrutable predestination Paul so celebrates is most alien to Scripture and to all sound theologians.
source_text: Secundo et illud perpendendum, In praesenti nostra controversia Theologos nunquam per decretum praedestinationis intellexisse quodlibet placitum Divinae voluntatis de salute et exitio hominum, sub qualibet forma conceptum et in verbo revelatum. Nam si eo hoc vocabulum torquere libeat, ipsissimum decretum praedestinationis continebitur illis verbis Matth. xxv. 34. &c. Dicet Rex iis qui sunt ad dextram, Venite benedicti Patris mei, possidete regnum paratum vobis a jactis mundi fundamentis. Esurivi enim et dedistis mihi quo vescerer, &c. Dicet iis qui ad sinistram erunt, Abite maledicti in ignem aeternum, qui paratus est diabolo et angelis ejus. Esurivi enim, et non dedistis mihi quo vescerer, &c. Exprimetur etiam praedestinationis decretum et in illis ad Rom. ii. 6. Deus reddet unicuique secundum opera ipsius: iis quidem qui perstant, boni operis gloriam et honorem et immortalitatem: iis vero qui sunt contentiosi, et qui veritati non obtemperant, sed obtemperant injustitiae, reddetur excandescentia et ira, &c. In hisce enim et similibus locis, patefit nobis voluntas Dei de salute et exitio hominum, et tamen in hujusmodi decretis ponere illam altam et inscrutabilem praedestinationem quam Paulus cantopere celebrat et admiratur, est a sensu et sententia Scripturarum, atque omnium sanorum Theologorum alienissimum.
